findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch Response but this caller reads the Google client's `res.data` shape, so synced Google token refreshes cannot consume the endpoint response.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch Response with only access/expiry fields while this caller requires HubSpot's camelCase token object, so the new endpoint contract breaks HubSpot refreshes.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — The new refresh path calls prisma without importing it, so this module cannot build or run.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The code persists the SafeParse success wrapper instead of its data, so the stored Google credential no longer has top-level token fields after the first refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Both computed schema keys collapse to the same literal object string, so synchronized expiry fields are stripped and refreshed credentials remain expired.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — An omitted rotated refresh token is replaced with the literal sentinel "refresh_token", so the next renewal submits an invalid credential instead of retaining the old token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync branch returns a raw Fetch Response while Google and HubSpot callers expect parsed provider objects, so enabling credential sync breaks their token refreshes.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is non-atomic, so concurrent first-time syncs can create duplicate credentials and leave consumers reading an arbitrary copy.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses the credential-sync endpoint and always posts a local refresh token, so synchronized access-token-only credentials cannot renew.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state merely echoes caller-controlled JSON instead of binding the callback to the initiating session, enabling login CSRF that can attach an attacker's provider account to a victim.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32 — Team credential creation checks only accepted membership rather than admin access, allowing ordinary members to install credentials that affect the whole team.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes a request with the header omitted pass the equality check, exposing arbitrary users' credential replacement whenever sharing is enabled.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync request authenticates only with enumerable user and app identifiers, so a reachable sync endpoint cannot distinguish Cal.com from attackers seeking OAuth access tokens.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch Response with only access/expiry fields while this caller requires HubSpot's camelCase token object, so the new endpoint contract breaks HubSpot refreshes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function is called and its return value is assigned to hubspotRefreshToken with type HubspotToken. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object (line 14 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts: 'return response'). However, the HubSpot code expects a HubspotToken object with properties like accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn (camelCase from HubSpot SDK). The fetch Response object doesn't have these properties - it has methods like .json(), .text(), etc. This would cause the subsequent code that accesses hubspotRefreshToken.refreshToken and hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn to fail or return undefined when credential sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is non-atomic, so concurrent first-time syncs can create duplicate credentials and leave consumers reading an arbitrary copy.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 57-91, there's a find-then-create pattern: first it queries for an existing credential (findFirst), then either updates or creates based on the result. This is indeed a race condition - if two concurrent requests come in for the same userId/appId combination when no credential exists, both could pass the findFirst check (returning null), and both would then attempt to create a new credential, resulting in duplicate entries. This is a real concurrency bug that could cause data integrity issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes a request with the header omitted pass the equality check, exposing arbitrary users' credential replacement whenever sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app-credential.ts lines 22-27: The check compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (empty string or undefined), then `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` would be `undefined` or `''`. If a request is sent without the header, `req.headers['calcom-webhook-secret']` would be `undefined`. So the comparison would be `undefined !== undefined` which is false, meaning the check would pass. However, if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set to empty string '', then the comparison would be `undefined !== ''` which is true, so it would fail. The real vulnerability is when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is completely unset (undefined), then both sides could be undefined and the check passes. This is a legitimate security concern - if the env var is not configured, the webhook endpoint becomes accessible without authentication when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync request authenticates only with enumerable user and app identifiers, so a reachable sync endpoint cannot distinguish Cal.com from attackers seeking OAuth access tokens.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the credential sync request only sends calcomUserId and appSlug in the POST body to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. There is no authentication header, secret, or signature included in this outbound request. While the webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) does verify CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for incoming requests, the outbound credential sync request to fetch tokens from an external endpoint has no authentication mechanism shown in the diff. This means if an attacker knows the sync endpoint URL, they could potentially request OAuth tokens by guessing user IDs and app slugs. This is a legitimate security concern about the authentication of the outbound sync request.
